description:
Comment 📺 to get a link to watch the new episode on YouTube!

Chasing that spark can feel exciting, but often it’s just a rush fueled by your nervous system reacting to familiar patterns—what some call the “trauma tingles.” It’s not a reliable sign of compatibility. Instead of focusing on the thrill, pay attention to whether the connection feels safe, steady, and secure. True compatibility is found in how someone makes you feel long-term, not just in the initial buzz.

The Sabrina Zohar Show EP 102 with @drscottlyons on the highs and lows in dating and relationships out now! Available on Spotify, Apple, YouTube and anywhere you listen to your podcasts! 

#datingadvice #podcast #trauma #thespark #traumaresponse #addiction
transcript: But if you're with someone and you're like, they're awesome, they're funny, and I enjoy being around them, but, you know, I hear all the time, like, the spark is missing. A.K.A. the trauma tingles. The spark is such a dangerous, like, you're chasing a feeling eventually that's going to go away. And the trauma tingles is the unconscious magnetism towards someone that is the familiar. Or it is something that is familiar enough that reactivates the familiar in you. I've had people say like, oh, so no one should have feelings on that first date. No, we're not talking about that. But if you're chasing that alone and you're not meeting the actual person, you're not actually in a relationship, you're chasing the sensation.
